name: Modern SEO - M1L2 Live Website Breakdown
body:
> Lesson · 2026-10-22

Part of: [Modern SEO - Module 1 Foundation and Diagnosis](lib:brain-modern-seo-module-1-foundation-and-diagnosis) | [Modern SEO Course](lib:brain-modern-seo-course) | [Learning Index](lib:brain-learning-index)

Note: this lesson was recorded in 4 parts (the main file plus `Lesson 2 continuation_1` to `continuation_3`, 17:01 total, about 10 minutes of real lesson). The continuation folders have transcripts only, no separate notes.md; the source notes.md already merges all four parts, so this note covers them all.

# Summary
A screen-share diagnosis of Kelley & Dawson Service, an HVAC company in Wichita, KS, for "air conditioning repair Wichita." The instructor sizes up the top 3 map results, picks a stuck target, runs a rank map, audits the GBP and homepage, finds four half-hour fixes, and recommends Core 30 content next.

# Key concepts
- **Primary category follows what people search.** For HVAC, "air conditioning repair" is "almost always the primary category we target," not "HVAC contractor."
- **Indexed page count as a size benchmark.** `site:domain.com` on the top 3 gave 39, 62 and 134 pages; his "completely blind" estimate was 60 to 90 pages to compete. The target had 10.
- **Choosing a target:** many reviews, weak ranking, primary category matching the keyword, close to the city. Reviews are harder to fix than basics.
- **Grid range matters.** A wide grid (25,577 m spacing) showed 0% top 3; a tighter grid (2,504 m) showed 8.28% top 3. Not ranking top 3 at your own address is "usually a pretty bad sign."
- **Compare Top 3% against competitors** (several were in the 18 to 34% range): that gap is the room to grow.
- **Do not change a primary category that is working.**
- **GBP activity does not replace basics.** The business posted and had 541 reviews, but basics were wrong.
- **Free quick wins as a sales tool** to earn a prospect's trust.

# Diagnostic steps
1. Search main keyword + city; open the top 3 map results.
2. `site:` each top 3 domain; record indexed page counts.
3. Pick a target from "More businesses"; `site:` its domain.
4. Run a grid rank map (LeadSnap shown); tighten the grid if needed; sort competitors by Top 3%.
5. Pull GBP data with GMB Everywhere; check the primary category and count services (had 7 or 8, wants 20 to 30).
6. Check homepage title tag and H1 for primary category + city; phone click-to-call and matching the GBP; reviews widget; GBP embed; affiliation links.
7. Test schema (validator.schema.org): only WebPage schema was present, no LocalBusiness.
8. List the quick fixes, then plan Core 30 content to close the page-count gap.

# The four quick fixes
Title tag, H1, LocalBusiness schema, more GBP services. "You could change those four things in a half hour."

# How this applies to TAG clients
- Run this diagnostic on [Pipeliners (Hub)](lib:brain-pipeliners-hub), [Alphalete Trenchless (Hub)](lib:brain-alphalete-trenchless-hub) and [Summit Plumbing Pros AZ (Hub)](lib:brain-summit-plumbing-pros-az-hub): keyword + city, `site:` the top 3 and the client, compare counts before any Core 30 planning.
- **Summit AZ phone match:** GHL call tracking swaps the displayed number in the browser; the real number (480) 447-7008 stays in the HTML and schema. Compare the HTML/schema number, not a screenshot, and never touch the tracking snippet.
- Count each client's [Google Business Profile](lib:brain-google-business-profile) services against the 20 to 30 target, adding only services the client really offers. Leave a primary category alone if it ranks well.
- LeadSnap is paid. Do not sign up without Kim's approval; check first whether [Search Atlas](lib:brain-search-atlas) can produce a grid rank map.
- All fixes go to Kim as copy-paste lists; client sites are read-only for Claude.

# Caveats and open questions
- Overlapping recordings and dead air between parts; content merged once.
- The 60 to 90 page estimate is a guess, not a rule. Air Source's 62 pages was spoken, not shown.
- The "H1" shown was not confirmed in page source.
